extracted.intended_audience: users of the PARI/GP library (mathematicians and computational number theorists) working with L-functions and modular forms
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted API documentation and operational constraints for PARI/GP routines manipulating L-functions and modular forms (initialization, evaluation, cost estimates, searches, and conversions). Targets developers and researchers using these library functions correctly and efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: lfunrootres: root number and residue computation
rubrics_metrics.description: When at most a single pole is allowed, lfunrootres computes both the root number and the residue (0 if no pole).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The function inspects the polar part to determine residues; the behaviour differs if there is a single pole versus more complicated polar structure (examples show single pole at 1, double pole cases). Use the library syntax GEN lfunrootres(GEN data, long bitprec).

rubrics_metrics.name: lfuntheta: m-th derivative evaluation and error bound
rubrics_metrics.description: lfuntheta(data, t, {m=0}) computes the m-th derivative at t of the theta function attached to the L-function given by data. The result is given with absolute error less than 2^{-B}, where B = realbitprecision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: data can be a standard L-function data or output of lfunthetainit. The theta function is defined by the specified Dirichlet-series/inverse-Mellin transform formula; in the modular-form case Θ(t)=2(f(it/N)−a(0)) and a(0)=−L(f,0). Use GEN lfuntheta(GEN data, GEN t, long m, long bitprec).

rubrics_metrics.name: lfunthetacost: cost estimation for theta evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: lfunthetacost(L, {tdom}, {m=0}) estimates the number of Fourier coefficients a(n) that would be computed for lfunthetainit(L,tdom,m) at current bit precision; also estimates cost of subsequent lfuntheta (which must compute that many gammamellininv values).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If L is already an Linit, tdom and m are ignored and should be omitted to get cost for that particular Linit. Domain restrictions apply to t (examples show domain error when arg t > 0.785...). Use long lfunthetacost0(GEN L, GEN tdom = NULL, long m, long bitprec).

rubrics_metrics.name: lfunthetainit: allowed t-domain descriptors and cone constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: lfunthetainit(L,{tdom},{m=0}) initializes evaluation of theta derivatives for t in domain tdom. By default t real, t ≥ 1. tdom may be a positive real ρ, a non-real complex number (compute at that t, and allows evaluation for any z with |z| ≥ |t| and |arg z| ≤ |arg t|), or a pair [ρ,α] meaning |t| ≥ ρ and |arg t| ≤ α.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must satisfy the cone constraint |2·arg z/d| < π/2 (and |2α/d| < π/2), where d is the degree of the Γ factor. Initialization (the T structure) speeds up multiple evaluations in the cone; domain errors occur otherwise (example: lfuntheta domain error when arg t > 0.785398163397448). Use GEN lfunthetainit(GEN L, GEN tdom = NULL, long m, long bitprec).

rubrics_metrics.name: lfuntwist: conductor coprimality requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: lfuntwist(L, chi) creates the Ldata structure of the twist of L by the primitive character attached to Dirichlet character chi. The conductor of the character must be coprime to the conductor of L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If conductors are not coprime the twist is not accepted; use GEN lfuntwist(GEN L, GEN chi).

rubrics_metrics.name: lfunzeros: naive zero-finding assumptions and divz parameter
rubrics_metrics.description: lfunzeros(L, lim, {divz=8}) computes an ordered list of zeros of L(s) on the critical line in the interval specified by lim using a naive algorithm which may miss zeros: it assumes two consecutive zeros at height T ≥ 1 differ by at least 2π/ω where ω := divz·(d·log(T/2π) + d + 2·log(N/(π/2)^d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase divz (integral > 8) for a finer search mesh. The algorithm also assumes all zeros are simple except possibly at s=k/2 and that there are no poles in the search interval; a possible zero at s=k/2 is repeated according to multiplicity. Use GEN lfunzeros(GEN L, GEN lim, long divz, long bitprec).

rubrics_metrics.name: lfunzeros: Linit domain requirement for reliable detection near top boundary
rubrics_metrics.description: If you pass an Linit argument to lfunzeros, ensure the algorithm has L = lfuninit(Ldata, [T+1]) where T is the upper bound of lim: this allows detection of zeros near T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure the Linit domain contains [1, T+1]; a domain [0, T] is not sufficient. The algorithm assumes any multiple zero at s=k/2 has order ≤ maximal derivation order allowed by the Linit; increasing that derivation order in Linit is costly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supported modular form spaces (mfinit): space flags and decomposition
rubrics_metrics.description: mfinit initializes modular form spaces: full Mk(Γ0(N),χ) (flag 4), cuspidal Sk (flag 1), Eisenstein Ek (flag 3) with Mk = Ek ⊕ Sk, newspace Snew_k (flag 0) and oldspace Sold_k (flag 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The resulting mf structure contains a basis accessible via mfbasis; mfeigenbasis returns the eigenbasis of the newspace only (even if a larger space was requested). Fourier coefficients of basis elements lie in the cyclotomic field Q(χ) and are given algebraically (rational numbers or t_POLMODs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalized modular forms: internal format and caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Modular forms are represented in an internal format allowing mfcoefs to compute arbitrarily many Fourier coefficients; coefficients are given algebraically and mfparams can recover level, weight, character and field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some creation/operations (derivation/integration, E2, eta quotients, quotients) may produce objects that are not true modular forms; the library does not attempt to check modularity. When a function's documentation does not state it applies to generalized modular forms, the output is undefined if the input is not a true modular form.

rubrics_metrics.name: getcache: cache reporting and growth policy
rubrics_metrics.description: getcache() returns name, size, number of cache misses since last extension, largest cache miss and size in bytes for various auto-growing caches (Hurwitz class numbers, small integer factorizations, divisors, primitive dihedral forms, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caches start empty, are set to small defaults, grow on demand up to a maximal value and never decrease; they are freed only on exit. Use GEN getcache().

rubrics_metrics.name: lfunmf: mapping modular forms to L-functions and orbit handling
rubrics_metrics.description: lfunmf(mf, {F}) returns the L-functions corresponding to F (a modular form) or, if F omitted, the L-functions attached to all eigenforms in the new space: a vector whose length equals the number of Galois orbits of newforms, each entry being the vector of L-functions for the d complex embeddings of an orbit of dimension d over Q(χ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use GEN lfunmf(GEN mf, GEN F = NULL, long bitprec). Example usage shows concatenation of orbit vectors to obtain all attached L-functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: mfcoefs/mfcoef: coefficient extraction convention and indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: mfcoefs(F,n,{d=1}) computes [a[0], a[d], ..., a[nd]] of generalized modular form F (d positive, default 1); mfcoef(F,n) returns the n-th Fourier coefficient (the n+1-st component of mfcoefs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When F is a modular form space (mfinit output), mfcoefs returns the matrix whose columns give Fourier expansions of mfbasis(F). Coefficients are algebraic (rational or t_POLMODs). Use GEN mfcoefs(GEN F, long n, long d) and GEN mfcoef(GEN F, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: mfdiv: quotient validity at infinity
rubrics_metrics.description: mfdiv(F,G) divides two generalized modular forms assuming the quotient will not have poles at infinity; if quotient would have poles at infinity, use mfshift before dividing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ord(G) > ord(F) a domain error occurs (example shown). Use GEN mfdiv(GEN F, GEN G).

rubrics_metrics.name: mffrommetaquo: holomorphy and valuation rules for eta-quotients
rubrics_metrics.description: mffrommetaquo(eta, {flag=0}) returns the modular form corresponding to an eta quotient matrix eta. If valuation at infinity is fractional return 0. If the eta quotient is meromorphic, return 0 if flag=0; if flag≠0 return the eta quotient divided by q^{-v} if v<0 (i.e., with valuation 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 1×k vector is accepted instead of a factorization matrix. Use GEN mffrommetaquo(GEN eta, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: mffromlfun: recognize modular form space from an L-function
rubrics_metrics.description: mffromlfun(L) given an L-function representing a self-dual modular form returns [NK, space, v] where mf = mfinit(NK, space) is the modular form space containing the form and mftobasis(mf, v) represents it on the space basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If L has inexact complex coefficients, one can compute an eigenbasis for mf and check if one attached L-function is close to L; examples show comparing lfunan(L,10) vectors to detect match. Use GEN mffromlfun(GEN L, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: mfeigensearch: search parameters NK and AP semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: mfeigensearch(NK, {AP}) searches for normalized rational eigen cuspforms with quadratic character under restrictions on initial Fourier coefficients. NK = [N,k] (or vector of allowed levels); AP is list of [p,ap] where p prime and ap either an integer (coefficient must match) or Mod(a,b) (coefficient congruence modulo b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Result vector of newforms matching criteria sorted by increasing level then increasing |D|. Use GEN mfeigensearch(GEN NK, GEN AP = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: mfatkininit: Atkin–Lehner initialization and returned structure
rubrics_metrics.description: mfatkininit(mf,Q) initializes data for Atkin–Lehner operator W_Q for primitive divisor Q of level N in mf. Returns 4-component vector [mfB, CM, C, mf].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: mfB encodes the target modular form space (or 0 if character does not change), CM is M·C (matrix of W_Q multiplied by normalizing constant) with polmod coefficients in Q(χ), C is the complex normalization constant (if rational A, C=1). Use GEN mfatkininit(GEN mf, long Q, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: mfatkineigenvalues: Atkin–Lehner eigenvalues grouped by orbit and rounding
rubrics_metrics.description: mfatkineigenvalues(mf, Q) outputs Atkin–Lehner eigenvalues of w_Q on the new space, grouped by orbit. If χ is trivial or quadratic modulo N/Q, the result is rounded and eigenvalues are ±i^k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To get eigenvalues on spaces larger than the new space compute [mfB,M,C]=mfatkininit and find roots of charpoly(M)/C. Coefficients may be polmods and must be embedded to C before root-finding when needed. Use GEN mfatkineigenvalues(GEN mf, long Q, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: mfbasis: basis ordering for full space
rubrics_metrics.description: mfbasis(NK,{space=4}) returns a basis of the corresponding subspace of Mk(Γ0(N),χ). If space is the full space Mk, the output is first a basis of Eisenstein space then a basis of the cuspidal space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain eigenforms use mfeigenbasis. NK can be the output of mfinit; use GEN mfbasis(GEN NK, long space).

rubrics_metrics.name: mfeigenbasis: eigenbasis is for newspace and efficiency note
rubrics_metrics.description: mfeigenbasis(mf) returns the vector of eigenforms for the space mf; the eigenforms are expressed internally as algebraic linear combinations of mfbasis(mf) and individually expanding many coefficients for eigenforms is inefficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To expand many eigenforms efficiently, compute M = mfcoefs(mf, N) once and multiply by mftobasis(mf, B[i]) to obtain expansions faster. Use GEN mfeigenbasis(GEN mf).

rubrics_metrics.name: mfconductor: minimal defining level
rubrics_metrics.description: mfconductor(mf, F) gives the smallest level on which modular form F (in cuspidal space mf) is defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns a long value giving the conductor; use long mfconductor(GEN mf, GEN F).

rubrics_metrics.name: mfcuspval/mfcusps/mfcuspwidth: cusp data conventions and return types
rubrics_metrics.description: mfcusps(N) lists cusps of Γ0(N) as rationals a/b with b|N. mfcuspval(mf,F,cusp) returns the valuation of F at cusp (∞ or rational), returning either a rational number or ∞ if F=0; if Q(F)≠Q(χ) returns a vector of valuations for each complex embedding. mfcuspwidth(N,cusp) returns the cusp width.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: mfcuspisregular(NK,cusp) determines if given cusp is regular. Use GEN mfcusps(GEN N), GEN mfcuspval(GEN mf, GEN F, GEN cusp, long bitprec) and long mfcuspwidth(GEN N, GEN cusp).

rubrics_metrics.name: mfembed: embeddings when Q(f) larger than Q(χ) and application to coefficient vectors
rubrics_metrics.description: mfembed(f, {v}) returns embeddings of Q(f) induced over Q(χ) or applies embeddings to v. If Q(f)=Q(χ) return single canonical embedding; if Q(f)>Q(χ) return [Q(f):Q(χ)] induced embeddings attached to complex roots of s(P). If v omitted returns embeddings; if v provided apply embeddings coefficientwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: f may be an eigenform produced by mfeigenbasis when Q(f)>Q(χ). Also allow mfinit output instead of f for Q(χ) single embedding. Use GEN mfembed0(GEN f, GEN v = NULL, long prec). Examples illustrate lifting polmods and applying embeddings to coefficient vectors; care must be taken when substituting field generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: mfeval: numerical evaluation and error bound; embedding multiplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: mfeval(mf,F,vtau) computes numerical value(s) of F at vtau with absolute error < 2^{-B} where B=realbitprecision. If Q(F)>Q(χ) it returns a vector of d=[Q(F):Q(χ)] embedded values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To maximize imaginary part of the argument the function computes (f|_k γ)(γ^{-1}·τ) for a suitable γ (possibly not in Γ0(N)), using mfslashexpansion when necessary. Use GEN mfeval(GEN mf, GEN F, GEN vtau, long bitprec).

rubrics_metrics.name: mffromqf: theta correspondence and half-integral weights
rubrics_metrics.description: mffromqf(Q,{P}) given an even integral positive definite quadratic form Q and spherical polynomial P, computes [mf, F, v] where F is the theta function corresponding to (Q,P), mf its modular form space and v the coefficients in mfbasis(mf). Odd dimensions supported correspond to half-integral weight forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The function can compute large coefficients fast (examples show massive coefficients computed quickly). Use GEN mffromqf(GEN Q, GEN P = NULL).
